summary: Phase 147L.1 was authorized, following Phase 147L's AESIC-001 VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS verdict, to perform a strictly bounded repair of AESIC-001's two Major, internally-inconsistent findings -- contract-repair only, no production code, no schema change, no runtime change, no amendment to any contract other than AESIC-001. Finding 1 (stage_1_outcome_ref, AESIC-REQ-057, section 8.6, defined to make both outcomes retrievable, contradicting AESIC-REQ-064/080's unconditional guarantee that Stage 1's outcome is never persisted anywhere) is repaired by redefining stage_1_outcome_ref (new AESIC-REQ-118) as an inline, verbatim, byte-for-byte embedded copy of Stage 1's own outcome, evaluation_id, and timestamp, written directly into the AER's own document body -- never a pointer to separately-durable state. AESIC-REQ-064/080 are clarified, not weakened, to confirm never-persisted has always meant never persisted as its own, independently-addressable artifact. This simultaneously closes Phase 147L's Informational Finding 4 by stating the previously-unstated evaluation_id/stage_1_outcome_ref relationship. Finding 2 (Stage 2's O_CREAT|O_EXCL, package_id-only idempotency mechanism, AESIC-REQ-019/053/078, structurally unable to accommodate section 11.2's restart-matrix rows requiring a changed-input retry to supersede with a new, disclosed record) is repaired by a new two-tier storage model (new AESIC-REQ-119): AERs stored under a collision-free compound (package_id, evaluation_id) key, with a separate, atomically-updated package_id-keyed canonical pointer index for ordinary lookup. AESIC-REQ-023 is repaired to state the complete recompute-compare-then-(no-op-or-supersede) decision procedure; new AESIC-REQ-120 discloses the canonical pointer's own deliberate, data-safe last-write-wins concurrency semantics, mirroring IWPC-001's own already-frozen precedent. This simultaneously closes Phase 147L's Minor Finding 3 by defining the previously-unspecified inputs-unchanged equality procedure (new AESIC-REQ-121) and its one-additional-read performance-budget cost (AESIC-REQ-102, repaired). Four new requirements (AESIC-REQ-118 through 121) were added; eleven existing requirements were repaired or clarified in place with their identity preserved; zero requirements were renumbered or reused; 106 of 117 v1.0 requirements remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Every architectural invariant named in this phase's own governing prompt (AES ownership, Registry ownership, evaluator purity, disclosure-only semantics, replay architecture, persistence architecture, AER architecture, lifecycle architecture, Stage 2 supersession principle) is confirmed preserved by independent cross-check against the repaired text. Zero amendments to AEM-001, AEMIC-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, or CHGR-001 are required, independently reconfirming AESIC-REQ-113 unchanged. Overall Verdict: AESIC-001 v1.1 REPAIRED. Full detail in docs/contracts/AESIC-001-authority-evaluation-service-integration-contract.md (sections 25-28) and docs/verification/PHASE_147L1_CONTRACT_REPAIR.md.

validation_results.name: phase_147l1_research_grounding
validation_results.result: Directly re-read the complete AESIC-001 v1.0 contract text (1247 lines, all 24 sections) and the complete Phase 147L Independent Verification report (386 lines) in full, including its section 2 independent reconstruction, section 5 requirement verification matrix, sections 8/9/11 replay/persistence/observability adversarial analysis, and section 14 findings, to ground both repairs in the exact contradiction each finding identified rather than a paraphrase of it.

validation_results.name: phase_147l1_root_cause_analysis
validation_results.result: Finding 1's root cause traced to AESIC-001's own naming discipline: every other _ref field in v1.0 genuinely points to separately-durable state, but stage_1_outcome_ref was drafted by the same convention without accounting for AESIC-REQ-064/080's unconditional prohibition on Stage 1 persistence. Finding 2's root cause traced to AESIC-REQ-019 directly borrowing PublicationRecordStore.commit_publication's O_CREAT|O_EXCL pattern, which correctly encodes at-most-once-ever semantics for Publication but silently imported that same semantics into Stage 2 evaluation, whose own independently-drafted restart matrix (section 11.2) already required a richer, supersession-capable semantics the two halves of AESIC-001 v1.0 were never checked against each other at freeze time.

validation_results.name: phase_147l1_repair_verification
validation_results.result: Re-read every repaired and new requirement (AESIC-REQ-019/023/053/056/057/064/078/080/081/098/102/118/119/120/121) against every other requirement it interacts with: confirmed Finding 1 does not recur (stage_1_outcome_ref's embedded-copy shape satisfies both-outcomes-retrievable without requiring durable Stage-1-only storage AESIC-REQ-064/080 forbid); confirmed Finding 2 does not recur (the compound-key store can now write a genuinely new, distinct, immutable record on supersession without violating AESIC-REQ-054/082); confirmed the repair introduces no new contradiction (AESIC-REQ-119's two-tier model checked against AESIC-REQ-078's exactly-one-artifact-type claim; AESIC-REQ-120's last-write-wins pointer checked against AESIC-REQ-104's concurrent-idempotency guarantee); confirmed no change fell outside the declared scope (full requirement change list cross-checked against the No-Go Boundary).
